reconcile.note: Keil & Delitzsch answer the self-praise objection by treating Numbers 12:3 as inspired, objective testimony about Moses rather than boastful self-display.

discrepancy.note: Paine argues no self-respecting author would call himself meeker than all men, so Moses cannot be the Pentateuch's author.

quotes.text: Numbers xii. 3: " Now the man Moses was very Meek , above all the men which were on the face of the earth ." If Moses said this of himself, instead of being the meekest of men, he was one of the most vain and arrogant coxcombs … because to boast of meekness is the reverse of meekness, and is a lie in sentiment .
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), ch. I, on Numbers 12:3.
